documents.title: API Authentication & OAuth2 Standards
documents.content:
# API Authentication & OAuth2 Standards

All Kestrel Cloud backend services must authenticate incoming requests using **Entra ID OAuth 2.0 / OIDC** bearer tokens.

## Mandatory Validation Rules
1. Verify RS256 signatures against the tenant JWKS endpoint (`iss`, `aud`, `exp`).
2. Extract immutable user identity strictly from the `oid` claim—never rely on `sub` or mutable email/UPN claims.
3. Enforce required delegated scope (`access_as_user`) on user-facing endpoints.
4. Resolve group memberships via On-Behalf-Of (OBO) Graph calls and **fail closed** on any token or directory lookup error.

documents.title: Incident Severity Classification Matrix
documents.content:
# Incident Severity Classification Matrix

Consistent severity classification ensures rapid escalation across all Kestrel Cloud teams.

## Levels
- **SEV-1 (Critical):** Complete outage of core APIs, data loss, security breach, or unauthorized cross-tenant/cross-group data exposure. Page immediately; postmortem required within 48 hours.
- **SEV-2 (High):** Significant degradation (`> 5%` error rate or `> 2x` latency SLA) with no workaround. Page primary on-call.
- **SEV-3 (Medium):** Minor feature impairment or single non-critical job failure. Handle during business hours.
- **SEV-4 (Low):** Cosmetic issues or minor documentation gaps. Track in backlog.

documents.title: Kubernetes Resource Quotas & Autoscaling
documents.content:
# Kubernetes Resource Quotas & Autoscaling

Standardized resource requests and HorizontalPodAutoscaler (HPA) settings prevent noisy-neighbor CPU throttling.

## Baseline Defaults
- Always set `requests.cpu == limits.cpu`? No—set `requests.cpu` to P50 usage and omit `limits.cpu` for latency-sensitive APIs, while setting `requests.memory == limits.memory` to prevent unexpected OOM kills.
- Configure HPA target CPU utilization at `65%` with `minReplicas: 2` across at least 2 availability zones.
- Include a `PodDisruptionBudget` (`minAvailable: 1`) on all stateless deployments.

documents.title: Observability: Logging & Tracing Standards
documents.content:
# Observability: Logging & Tracing Standards

All services emit structured JSON logs and OpenTelemetry traces to our central collector.

## Logging Rules
- Include `trace_id`, `span_id`, `service`, `env`, and `tenant_id` on every log line.
- **Never** log bearer tokens, API keys, PII, or raw document contents at `INFO` or `DEBUG` in production.
- Use `WARNING` for recoverable downstream retries and `ERROR` only for actionable failures.

## Tracing
Propagate W3C `traceparent` headers across all HTTP and Kafka boundaries.

documents.title: PostgreSQL Connection Pooling Guidelines
documents.content:
# PostgreSQL Connection Pooling Guidelines

All production Python services connect to PostgreSQL through **PgBouncer** in `transaction` pooling mode.

## Configuration Standards
- Set SQLAlchemy/psycopg client pool `max_size = 10` per pod to avoid exhausting PgBouncer slots.
- Always configure `statement_timeout = 5000` (5 seconds) on interactive API connections.
- Avoid session-level prepared statements or temporary tables when using transaction pooling.
- Monitor `pgbouncer_pools_cl_waiting` in Grafana; alert if waiting clients `> 20` for 3 minutes.

documents.title: Secret Management & Key Rotation Policy
documents.content:
# Secret Management & Key Rotation Policy

Secrets must never be committed to Git or stored in plaintext environment files in shared environments.

## Policy Requirements
- Production secrets live in **Azure Key Vault / HashiCorp Vault** and are injected via CSI driver at pod startup.
- Client secrets (`API_CLIENT_SECRET`), webhook HMAC keys, and database passwords rotate every **90 days**.
- If a secret is accidentally pushed to any branch, revoke it immediately, purge history if needed, and file a `SEV-1` security incident.

# Service-Level Objectives (SLO) Framework

Every Tier-1 service defines explicit Availability and Latency SLOs tracked over a 28-day rolling window.

## Standard Targets
- **Availability:** `99.95%` successful non-5xx responses (`21.6 minutes` monthly error budget).
- **Latency:** `p95 < 250 ms` for synchronous REST endpoints; `p99 < 1,000 ms` for RAG retrieval queries.

## Error Budget Policy
When a service burns `> 50%` of its monthly error budget in 7 days, feature launches pause in favor of reliability hardening.

# Billing Cycle Reconciliation Job

The nightly **Billing Reconciliation Job** runs at 02:00 UTC to verify that internal `invoices` match settled transactions from external settlement reports.

## Job Stages
- **Extract:** Pull previous day's CSV settlement files from S3 bucket `kestrel-settlements-prod`.
- **Match:** Join on `payment_intent_id` and compare `net_amount_cents`, `fee_cents`, and `currency`.
- **Discrepancy Triage:** Any delta `> $0.01` opens an automated Jira ticket in project `PAYOPS` and emits metric `reconciliation_mismatch_count`.

## SLA
Reconciliation must complete before 05:00 UTC so Finance can close daily revenue dashboards.

documents.title: Invoice PDF Rendering Pipeline
documents.content:
# Invoice PDF Rendering Pipeline

`invoice-renderer` generates localized PDF invoices for enterprise tenants using a sandboxed Chromium headless pool.

## Architecture
- **Trigger:** Consumes `invoice.finalized` events from `payments.invoices.v1`.
- **Templating:** Renders HTML from versioned Jinja2 templates with tax line items and tenant VAT IDs.
- **Storage:** Uploads immutable PDFs to `s3://kestrel-invoices-archive/{tenant_id}/{year}/{invoice_id}.pdf` with Object Lock enabled.

## Performance Limits
Each worker pod caps concurrent renders at 4 tabs to keep memory below `1.5 GiB`.

documents.title: Ledger Service Architecture
documents.content:
# Ledger Service Architecture

The Kestrel Cloud **Ledger Service** implements an immutable, append-only double-entry accounting store backed by PostgreSQL.

## Core Concepts
- **Accounts:** Typed as `ASSET`, `LIABILITY`, `REVENUE`, or `EXPENSE`, scoped per tenant.
- **Journal Entries:** Every financial state transition creates a balanced pair of debit and credit `ledger_entries` sharing a `journal_id`.
- **Idempotency:** Callers must supply an `Idempotency-Key` header (UUIDv4). Keys are cached in Redis for 24 hours and persisted in `journal_idempotency_keys`.

## Consistency Guarantees
All balance checks run under `SERIALIZABLE` isolation for payout approvals, while read-only statement exports query the async read replica.

documents.content:
# Payment Gateway Failover Design

To maintain `99.99%` checkout availability, Team-A routes card authorizations across two independent payment processors: **PrimaryPay** (`85%` weight) and **BackupPay** (`15%` warm traffic).

## Circuit Breaker Rules
- Trip to `100%` BackupPay if PrimaryPay 5xx rate exceeds `3%` over a 2-minute sliding window or `p95` latency exceeds `2,500 ms`.
- Half-open probe sends `1%` synthetic health-check authorizations every 60 seconds before restoring primary traffic.

## Token Portability
Card tokens are stored in our PCI-scoped vault (`kestrel-vault`) so failover requires zero customer re-entry.

documents.title: Postmortem: Double-Charge Incident Oct 14
documents.content:
# Postmortem: Double-Charge Incident Oct 14

**Date:** October 14 | **Severity:** SEV-1 | **Duration:** 23 minutes | **Author:** Team-A

## Summary
A retry storm in `billing-worker` caused 142 tenants to be charged twice for monthly seat overages.

## Root Cause
During a Redis failover, the idempotency key cache returned transient connection timeouts. The worker treated cache lookup errors as "key not seen" (fail-open) instead of aborting the charge attempt.

## Action Items
1. Change idempotency lookup to **fail-closed** on Redis errors (`PAY-412`, completed).
2. Add a unique partial index on `(tenant_id, billing_period, charge_type)` in `billing_db` (`PAY-415`, completed).
3. Automated refunds issued to all 142 affected accounts within 2 hours.

documents.title: Refund State Machine Specification
documents.content:
# Refund State Machine Specification

Refunds in `ledger-api` follow a strict deterministic finite state machine.

## States & Transitions
- `REQUESTED` -> `PENDING_GATEWAY` (once balance check passes)
- `PENDING_GATEWAY` -> `SUCCEEDED` | `FAILED`
- `FAILED` -> `MANUAL_REVIEW` (after 3 exponential backoff retries)

## Invariants
- Total refunded amount across all `SUCCEEDED` and `PENDING_GATEWAY` refunds for a charge must never exceed `original_charge_amount_cents`.
- Partial refunds emit a proportional credit memo entry in `ledger_entries`.

documents.title: Gateway Webhook Idempotency Spec
documents.content:
# Gateway Webhook Idempotency Spec

External payment processors occasionally deliver duplicate or out-of-order webhook events. Team-A's ingestion gateway enforces strict deduplication.

## Processing Pipeline
1. Verify HMAC-SHA256 signature header (`X-Gateway-Signature`) against the rotated secret in Vault.
2. Insert `(provider, event_id)` into `processed_webhook_events` with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`.
3. If inserted, enqueue the normalized payload onto Kafka topic `payments.webhooks.v2`; otherwise return `200 OK` immediately.

## Out-of-Order Handling
State transitions use monotonic sequence numbers (`event_created_at` + `state_version`) so stale `charge.pending` events never overwrite `charge.settled`.

# Cold-Start Ranking Fallback Design

New tenants with fewer than 50 indexed documents lack historical click signals for learned-to-rank models.

## Fallback Strategy
- Bypass the GBDT personalization layer when `tenant_doc_count < 50`.
- Rank purely by normalized Hybrid RRF score (`0.7 * dense_cosine + 0.3 * bm25`) plus recency boost (`half_life = 30 days`).
- Gradually blend behavioral features once a tenant crosses 500 recorded search impressions.

documents.content:
# Embedding Refresh Pipeline Spec

When Team-B upgrades the sentence embedding model, `embed-worker` re-embeds historical chunks without causing search downtime.

## Blue/Green Vector Columns
1. Add nullable `embedding_v2 vector(768)` alongside active `embedding_v1`.
2. Backfill batches of 500 chunks via Ray workers throttled to `40%` GPU utilization.
3. Build HNSW index on `embedding_v2` (`m=16, ef_construction=128`).
4. Flip feature flag `SEARCH_ACTIVE_EMBEDDING_COL=embedding_v2` and drop `embedding_v1` after 7 days.

documents.title: Feature Store Caching Strategy
documents.content:
# Feature Store Caching Strategy

`ranker-service` fetches document freshness, click-through priors, and popularity signals from Redis Cluster.

## Caching Rules
- **TTL:** Popularity counters use a 15-minute TTL with probabilistic early expiration to prevent thundering herds.
- **Compression:** Feature vectors are serialized as MessagePack + LZ4, reducing Redis memory footprint by `58%`.
- **Fallback:** On Redis timeout (`> 5 ms`), the ranker falls back to static default priors (`0.5`) so search availability is never blocked.

**Date:** November 02 | **Severity:** SEV-2 | **Duration:** 47 minutes | **Author:** Team-B

Newly uploaded documents took up to 45 minutes to appear in search results due to consumer lag on `search.ingest.v1`.

documents.title: Query Rewriter & Synonym Expansion
documents.content:
# Query Rewriter & Synonym Expansion

`query-rewriter` normalizes user queries before vector and BM25 retrieval.

## Pipeline Steps
- **Spell Correction:** SymSpell dictionary built from domain-neutral technical terms (max edit distance 2).
- **Acronym Expansion:** Expands common engineering acronyms (e.g., `k8s -> kubernetes`, `pg -> postgres`) into weighted OR clauses for BM25.
- **Latency Budget:** Total rewrite step must complete in `< 8 ms` p99; if exceeded, pass raw query straight to retrieval.

documents.title: Relevance Evaluation Benchmark Report
documents.content:
# Relevance Evaluation Benchmark Report

**Benchmark Suite:** Kestrel-Eval-v3 (1,200 annotated queries across 8 domains)

## Results Summary
| Configuration | Recall@10 | NDCG@10 | p95 Latency |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| BM25 Only | 0.71 | 0.64 | 18 ms |
| Dense Vector Only | 0.83 | 0.76 | 34 ms |
| Hybrid (RRF + Cross-Encoder) | **0.92** | **0.87** | 68 ms |

## Key Takeaway
Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF, `k=60`) followed by a lightweight cross-encoder reranker on top-25 candidates yields the best accuracy-to-latency tradeoff.

documents.title: Search Indexer Sharding Architecture
documents.content:
# Search Indexer Sharding Architecture

Kestrel Cloud's **Search Indexer** partitions tenant corpora across 16 logical shards using consistent hashing on `tenant_id`.

## Design Highlights
- **Routing:** `search-router` computes `murmur3(tenant_id) % 16` to target only the relevant shard, avoiding scatter-gather fanout for single-tenant queries.
- **Hot-Tenant Isolation:** Enterprise tenants exceeding `5M` chunks are promoted to dedicated isolated shards via dynamic routing table entries in etcd.
- **Compaction:** Background merge workers compact tombstone segments nightly at 03:00 UTC.

3. **Ingestion Isolation:** Eliminate noisy-neighbor index lag via dedicated bulk-import queues.
